parts.prompt: Directions: Suppose your university newspaper is inviting submissions from the students for its coming edition on future applications of robots on campus. You are now to write an essay for submission. You will have 30 minutes to write the essay. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.

reference.essayTranslation:
随着科技的飞速发展，机器人已逐渐应用于各个行业和领域。因此，在我看来，未来机器人也将融入校园生活，重塑学生的日常体验。

首先，机器人将成为学习和科研的得力助手。在实验室中，机器人能够完成重复性操作并准确记录实验数据，从而提高实验的整体效率。此外，机器人还能处理各种校园事务。例如，智能配送机器人可把快递包裹或餐食送到宿舍，而清洁机器人则能让校园保持整洁。最后但同样重要的是，机器人可以创造一个更安全的环境。安保机器人可以在夜间巡逻，探测烟雾或异常声响，并立即向控制中心发出警报。

总之，机器人将为未来的校园生活带来极大的便利与效率。毫无疑问，它们会让我们的校园生活更加丰富多彩。
reference.modelEssay:
With the rapid development of technology, robots have gradually been applied in various industries and fields. Consequently, robots, for my part, will also be introduced into campus life in the future, reshaping students’ daily experiences.

To begin with, robots will become powerful assistants in learning and research. In laboratories, robots are able to finish repetitive operations and record experimental data accurately, which improves the overall efficiency of experiments. In addition, robots can handle various campus affairs. For instance, intelligent delivery robots can transport packages or meals to dormitories, while robotic cleaners keep the campus tidy. Last but not least, robots can create a safer environment. Security robots can patrol at night, detect smoke or abnormal sounds, and then send alerts to the control center immediately.

To sum up, robots will bring great convenience and efficiency to future campuses. There is no doubt that they will make our campus life more colorful.

reference.shenTi: 作文要求以“机器人在未来校园中的应用”为话题展开论述。首段点明科技发展背景，引出“机器人将融入校园生活，重塑日常体验”的核心观点。主体段围绕机器人在校园中的应用场景进行分层论述。一是强调机器人在学习与科研场景的辅助作用，有助于提升学术效率；二是阐述机器人在校园日常事务中的应用，如物资配送、校园卫生等，为师生提供便利；三是说明机器人在校园安全管理中的功能，如夜间巡逻、隐患预警等，筑牢校园安全防线。最后一段总结全文，重申机器人对校园的积极影响。

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: She was born months after the end of World War I.
options.textZhGloss: 她出生于第一次世界大战结束数月之后。

options.textEn: She has been living in her house throughout her life.
options.textZhGloss: 她一生都住在这栋房子里。

options.textEn: She suffered a great deal during the Second World War.
options.textZhGloss: 她在第二次世界大战期间遭受了很多苦难。

options.textEn: She is a 102-year-old woman living in Somerset Village.
options.textZhGloss: 她是居住在萨默塞特村的一位102岁老人。

distractors: 录音开头提到南希·吉福德正在出售她从两岁起就一直居住的房子，而非一生都住在这栋房子里，故排除B)项；录音只提到南希·吉福德在这栋房子里经历了第二次世界大战(having lived in it through the Second World War)，但并未提及她在第二次世界大战期间遭受了很多苦难，C)项属于无中生有，故排除；D)项中的102年是南希·吉福德在房子里居住的时长，且录音开头点明她是104岁(A 104-year-old woman)，D)项与录音内容不符，故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report One）
evidence.quote: Nancy Gifford was born months after the end of the First World War and spent 102 years living in her three-bedroom house in the Somerset Village of Street.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 A)。句[1]提到,南希·吉福德出生于第一次世界大战结束数月之后。A)项对应录音内容,故为答案。其中 was born months after the end of 为录音原词复现,World War I 对应录音中的 the First World War。
干扰项排除 录音开头提到南希·吉福德正在出售她从两岁起就一直居住的房子，而非一生都住在这栋房子里，故排除B)项；录音只提到南希·吉福德在这栋房子里经历了第二次世界大战(having lived in it through the Second World War)，但并未提及她在第二次世界大战期间遭受了很多苦难，C)项属于无中生有，故排除；D)项中的102年是南希·吉福德在房子里居住的时长，且录音开头点明她是104岁(A 104-year-old woman)，D)项与录音内容不符，故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 关于南希·吉福德,新闻报道中提到了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: She has been persuaded by the estate agent.
options.textZhGloss: 她被房产经纪人劝说卖房。

options.textEn: She needs the money badly for her health.
options.textZhGloss: 她因为健康问题而急需用钱。

options.textEn: She is leaving Glastonbury Village.
options.textZhGloss: 她将离开格拉斯顿伯里村。

options.textEn: She is moving to a nursing home.
options.textZhGloss: 她将要搬去养老院。

distractors: 录音未提及房产经纪人劝她卖房,故排除 A)项;录音只提到健康问题是她搬家的原因,但未提及她因为健康问题而急需用钱,B)项属于过度解读,故排除;格拉斯顿伯里是养老院所在地,她是搬去这里,而非离开,C)项与录音内容相悖,故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report One）
evidence.quote: Mrs Gifford is selling the house and moving to a nursing home in nearby Glastonbury because of her health.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 D)。句[2]提到,吉福德夫人打算卖掉房子,搬到附近格拉斯顿伯里的一家养老院,原因是她的身体状况不佳。D)项是对录音中 moving to a nursing home 的原词复现,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音未提及房产经纪人劝她卖房,故排除 A)项;录音只提到健康问题是她搬家的原因,但未提及她因为健康问题而急需用钱,B)项属于过度解读,故排除;格拉斯顿伯里是养老院所在地,她是搬去这里,而非离开,C)项与录音内容相悖,故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 吉福德夫人为何要出售这栋房子?

items.groupHeader: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: The navy's timely arrival.
options.textZhGloss: 海军及时抵达。

options.textEn: His rich sailing experience.
options.textZhGloss: 他丰富的航海经验。

options.textEn: The word HELP written on the boat.
options.textZhGloss: 写在船上的单词“HELP”。

options.textEn: His use of a mirror to send a signal.
options.textZhGloss: 他利用镜子发出信号。

distractors: 海军是最终实施救援的一方,但录音并未说海军及时抵达是男子获救的关键,故排除 A)项;录音未提及男子有丰富的航海经验,故排除 B)项;利用镜子发出信号是男子中途尝试的求救手段,但这只是辅助行为,不是他获救的关键,故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report Two）
evidence.quote: The man, 47, wrote the word HELP in English on the boat, which was key to his rescue.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 C)。句[3]提到,这名 47 岁男子在船上写下了英文单词“HELP”,这成为他获救的关键。C)项是对录音中 wrote the word HELP in English on the boat 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 海军是最终实施救援的一方,但录音并未说海军及时抵达是男子获救的关键,故排除 A)项;录音未提及男子有丰富的航海经验,故排除 B)项;利用镜子发出信号是男子中途尝试的求救手段,但这只是辅助行为,不是他获救的关键,故排除 D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 新闻报道称,什么对该男子的获救起到了关键作用?

items.groupHeader: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: He lost all consciousness.
options.textZhGloss: 他完全失去了意识。

options.textEn: He was in good condition.
options.textZhGloss: 他身体状况良好。

options.textEn: He was too distressed to pick himself up.
options.textZhGloss: 他悲痛消沉,无法振作。

options.textEn: He entirely abandoned himself to despair.
options.textZhGloss: 他彻底陷入绝望。

distractors: 录音未提及他失去意识以及悲痛消沉，A)项和C)项属于无中生有，故均排除；录音提到男子尝试多种求救方法：在船上写下英文单词HELP（wrote the word “HELP” in English on the boat）、用布收集雨水（collected rainwater with a cloth）、生火发出求救信号（light a fire to send a distress signal）以及用镜子发出信号（signaled with a mirror），这一系列自救行为表明他并非陷入绝望，故排除D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report Two）
evidence.quote: He was found in good health but had lost weight.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 B)。句[4]提到,他被发现时健康状况良好,但体重减轻了。B)项是对录音中 was found in good health 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音未提及他失去意识以及悲痛消沉，A)项和C)项属于无中生有，故均排除；录音提到男子尝试多种求救方法：在船上写下英文单词HELP（wrote the word “HELP” in English on the boat）、用布收集雨水（collected rainwater with a cloth）、生火发出求救信号（light a fire to send a distress signal）以及用镜子发出信号（signaled with a mirror），这一系列自救行为表明他并非陷入绝望，故排除D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 我们可以了解到这名男子获救时的什么信息?

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: Their efforts to provide social services have been ignored.
options.textZhGloss: 它们为提供社会服务所做的努力被忽视了。

options.textEn: They have been criticized by the Denver school board.
options.textZhGloss: 它们遭到了丹佛校董事会的批评。

options.textEn: They have taken various steps to get more funding.
options.textZhGloss: 它们采取了多种措施以争取更多的经费。

options.textEn: Their enrollment has been on a noticeable decline.
options.textZhGloss: 它们的入学人数已出现明显的下降趋势。

distractors: 录音提到的是预算减少意味着无法再提供同样的心理健康支持、社交和情感服务（the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services），并非学校为提供社会服务所做的努力被忽视了，故排除 A) 项；B) 项和 C) 项在录音中均未提及，故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report Three）
evidence.quote: The board of Denver public schools is set to close several elementary and middle schools to make up for a decreased budget caused by declining enrollment.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 D)。句[5]提到,丹佛公立学校董事会计划关闭几所小学和中学,以弥补因入学人数下降而导致的预算减少。由此可知,丹佛将要关闭的小学和中学的入学人数已出现下降趋势。D)项是对录音中 declining enrollment 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音提到的是预算减少意味着无法再提供同样的心理健康支持、社交和情感服务（the decreased budget means it cannot provide the same mental health supports, social and emotional services），并非学校为提供社会服务所做的努力被忽视了，故排除 A) 项；B) 项和 C) 项在录音中均未提及，故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 关于在丹佛将要关闭的小学和中学,我们了解到了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: Approve criteria for closing schools with decreased funding.
options.textZhGloss: 通过针对经费缩减而关停学校的标准。

options.textEn: Enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students.
options.textZhGloss: 小学和中学的入学人数将减少3000人。

options.textEn: Decide which elementary and middle schools to close.
options.textZhGloss: 确定要关停哪些小学和中学。

options.textEn: Alter its per-pupil funding policy on a rational basis.
options.textZhGloss: 基于合理依据修改按人头拨款政策。

distractors: 录音中提到学校董事会通过了关闭学校的标准(The school board approved criteria to close schools)，这是已经发生了的事情，而非未来三年内会发生，A)项时间范围错误，故排除；录音中明确提到具体关停学校名单会在未来几天公布(The specific schools will be announced in the coming days)，而不是未来三年才决定，故排除C)项；录音中提到学区是按人头拨款，但录音并未提及要修改这一政策，故排除D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report Three）
evidence.quote: In the next three years, the district expects to enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students, it said.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 B)。句[6]提到,该校区表示,在未来三年内,预计小学和中学的入学人数将减少3000人。B)项是对录音中 enroll 3,000 fewer elementary and middle school students 的原词复现,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音中提到学校董事会通过了关闭学校的标准(The school board approved criteria to close schools)，这是已经发生了的事情，而非未来三年内会发生，A)项时间范围错误，故排除；录音中明确提到具体关停学校名单会在未来几天公布(The specific schools will be announced in the coming days)，而不是未来三年才决定，故排除C)项；录音中提到学区是按人头拨款，但录音并未提及要修改这一政策，故排除D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 丹佛校区预计在未来三年内会怎样?

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: To enable the district to remain competitive.
options.textZhGloss: 为了让校区保持竞争力。

options.textEn: To avoid a negative impact on its economy.
options.textZhGloss: 为了避免对当地经济造成负面影响。

options.textEn: To keep the district free of debt.
options.textZhGloss: 为了使校区不负债。

options.textEn: To obtain the expected funding.
options.textZhGloss: 为了获取预期的经费。

distractors: “让校区保持竞争力”和“当地经济”在录音中均未提及，故排除A)项和B)项；录音表明生源减少会导致拨款变少，“获取预期的经费”与录音逻辑相反，故排除D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（News Report Three）
evidence.quote: but in order for the district to stay out of debt, it's a step that needs to be taken," he said.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 C)。录音开头提到了丹佛校区计划关闭一些小学和中学,其后丹佛校区发言人在句[7]明确提到,为了让校区不陷入债务,这是必须采取的一步。必须采取的一步(a step that needs to be taken)即关闭一些学校。由此可知,C)项是对录音中 in order for the district to stay out of debt 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 “让校区保持竞争力”和“当地经济”在录音中均未提及，故排除A)项和B)项；录音表明生源减少会导致拨款变少，“获取预期的经费”与录音逻辑相反，故排除D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 根据校区发言人的说法,丹佛的一些学校为什么要关闭?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: To book tickets for a musical.
options.textZhGloss: 为了预定一场音乐剧的门票。

options.textEn: To enquire about the price of cats.
options.textZhGloss: 为了询问猫咪的价格。

options.textEn: To pay for her afternoon flight to London.
options.textZhGloss: 为了支付她下午飞往伦敦的航班费用。

options.textEn: To have her personal computer repaired.
options.textZhGloss: 为了找人修理她的个人电脑。

distractors: Cats 是音乐剧的名称,不是动物猫咪,B)项曲解了单词在录音中的含义,故排除;录音未提及女士飞往伦敦的航班,故排除 C)项;女士的电脑只是支付失败,录音中未提及找人修理她的个人电脑,故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation One）
evidence.quote: I've been trying to book tickets for the musical Cats in London on the evening of May the 28th.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 A)。女士在句[8]中提到,她一直在试着预订伦敦音乐剧《猫》在5月28日晚上的门票,但电
脑就是不接受她的银行卡付款。她已经试了三次了，但就是不能扣款。由此可知，女士订票失败，给男士打电话是为了预定一场音乐剧的门票。A)项是对录音中 to book tickets for the musical Cats 的同义转述，故为答案。
干扰项排除 Cats 是音乐剧的名称,不是动物猫咪,B)项曲解了单词在录音中的含义,故排除;录音未提及女士飞往伦敦的航班,故排除 C)项;女士的电脑只是支付失败,录音中未提及找人修理她的个人电脑,故排除 D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 女士为什么给男士打电话?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: He frequents the Lion Theatre.
options.textZhGloss: 他经常去莱昂剧院。

options.textEn: He knows how to sell things well.
options.textZhGloss: 他了解如何更好地卖东西。

options.textEn: He is a computer science expert.
options.textZhGloss: 他是计算机科学专家。

options.textEn: He is away on a business trip.
options.textZhGloss: 他正在外出差。

distractors: A)项和C)项在录音中均未提及,故排除;B)项是根据录音中女士提到的 And I know how quickly these things can sell out(而且我知道这些东西卖得有多快)设置的干扰,并非她的丈夫了解如何更好地卖东西,故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation One）
evidence.quote: My husband usually does all of these things, but he is in Italy on a business trip until next Thursday.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 D)。女士在句[9]提到,这些事情通常都是她丈夫做的,但他现在在意大利出差,下周四才回来。D)项是对录音中 he is in Italy on a business trip 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 A)项和C)项在录音中均未提及,故排除;B)项是根据录音中女士提到的 And I know how quickly these things can sell out(而且我知道这些东西卖得有多快)设置的干扰,并非她的丈夫了解如何更好地卖东西,故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 关于女士的丈夫,我们可以了解到什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: They are sold at a discount.
options.textZhGloss: 这些票打折出售。

options.textEn: They are in low demand.
options.textZhGloss: 这些票需求很低。

options.textEn: They are no longer available.
options.textZhGloss: 这些票已经买不到了。

options.textEn: They are not too expensive.
options.textZhGloss: 这些票价格不是太贵。

distractors: 录音未提及前排的票是否打折以及价格高低,故排除 A)项和 D)项;前排的票全部卖完,说明需求很高,B)项表述与录音相反,故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation One）
evidence.quote: all the tickets at the front are already sold out anyway, but I can offer you two upstairs near the middle.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 C)。句[10]明确提到,前排的所有票都已经卖完了。C)项是对录音内容的同义转述,故为答案。其中 no longer available 对应录音中的 sold out。
干扰项排除 录音未提及前排的票是否打折以及价格高低,故排除 A)项和 D)项;前排的票全部卖完,说明需求很高,B)项表述与录音相反,故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 关于前排的票,男士提到了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: Heights.
options.textZhGloss: 高度。

options.textEn: Circus.
options.textZhGloss: 马戏团。

options.textEn: Wild animals.
options.textZhGloss: 野生动物。

options.textEn: Dark nights.
options.textZhGloss: 漆黑的夜晚。

distractors: 录音未提及马戏团、野生动物以及漆黑的夜晚,故排除 B)项、C)项和 D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation One）
evidence.quote: I'm scared of heights, and you can never see anything if you are too high up anyway.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 A)。女士在句[11]中明确提到她害怕高处。A)项是录音中 heights 的原词复现,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音未提及马戏团、野生动物以及漆黑的夜晚,故排除 B)项、C)项和 D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 女士说她害怕什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: He finds it bothersome to reply.
options.textZhGloss: 他发现回复消息很麻烦。

options.textEn: He has switched off his phone.
options.textZhGloss: 他关掉了手机。

options.textEn: He hasn't got the time to text back.
options.textZhGloss: 他没时间回短信。

options.textEn: He doesn't know how to respond.
options.textZhGloss: 他不知道如何回复。

distractors: A)项和 C)项在录音中均未提及,故排除;男士是没看到短信,而不是不知道如何回复,故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation Two）
evidence.quote: Why haven't you answered my text messages lately? M: Oh, I didn't know you had sent any.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 B)。句[12-1]中,女士问男士最近为什么一直不回她的短信。男士在句[12-2]中回答道:“我差不多一周前就把手机关机了,从那以后就一直没再开机。”由此可知,B)项是对录音内容的同义转述,其中 switched off 对应录音中的 turned off,故为答案。
干扰项排除 A)项和 C)项在录音中均未提及,故排除;男士是没看到短信,而不是不知道如何回复,故排除 D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 这位男士最近为什么没有回复这位女士的短信?

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: His lack of sufficient sleep at night.
options.textZhGloss: 他夜间睡眠不足。

options.textEn: His addiction to mobile phone games.
options.textZhGloss: 他沉迷手机游戏。

options.textEn: His excessive use of the mobile phone.
options.textZhGloss: 他过度使用手机。

options.textEn: His high frequency of surfing the net.
options.textZhGloss: 他上网频率极高。

distractors: 录音未提及男士的夜间睡眠情况,故排除 A)项;录音中,男士明确否定自己沉迷于手机游戏,B)项与录音内容相悖,故排除;让男士震惊的是他使用手机的时长,而非上网频率,故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation Two）
evidence.quote: Well, I downloaded an app that recorded how much time I spent on my phone, and I was shocked to realize I was using my phone an average of eight hours a day.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 C)。男士在句[13]中提到,他下载了一个应用,能记录他在手机上花了多少时间,然后他震惊地意识到,他平均每天使用手机长达八个小时。最糟糕的一天是他使用了十二个小时。由此可知,男士震惊地意识到他过度使用手机。C)项是对录音内容的正确推断,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音未提及男士的夜间睡眠情况,故排除 A)项;录音中,男士明确否定自己沉迷于手机游戏,B)项与录音内容相悖,故排除;让男士震惊的是他使用手机的时长,而非上网频率,故排除 D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 这位男士下载了应用之后,震惊地意识到了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: Shopping online and paying for his purchases.
options.textZhGloss: 网上购物并线上付款。

options.textEn: Communicating with friends on social media.
options.textZhGloss: 在社交媒体上与朋友交流。

options.textEn: Exploring whatever content to his liking.
options.textZhGloss: 浏览他感兴趣的内容。

options.textEn: Sharing and posting pictures and videos.
options.textZhGloss: 分享并发布图片和视频。

distractors: 网上购物和线上付款是女士的行为,与男士无关,A)项混淆主体,故排除;C)项和D)项在录音中均未提及,故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation Two）
evidence.quote: I was spending too much time on social media, messaging friends, and commenting on other people's posts.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 B)。句[14]提到,男士花了太多时间在社交媒体上,给朋友发消息,以及评论别人的帖子。B)项是对录音内容的同义转述,故为答案。其中 Communicating with friends 对应录音中的 messaging friends; on social media 为原词复现。
干扰项排除 网上购物和线上付款是女士的行为,与男士无关,A)项混淆主体,故排除;C)项和D)项在录音中均未提及,故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 男士在手机上花费很多时间做什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: She prefers chatting with others online to meeting them.
options.textZhGloss: 相比线下见面,她更喜欢在线上和别人聊天。

options.textEn: There are few physical stores near where she lives.
options.textZhGloss: 她住的地方附近实体店很少。

options.textEn: Ordering meals online is a great convenience to her.
options.textZhGloss: 线上点餐对她来说十分方便。

options.textEn: She needs to talk with her friends and family far away.
options.textZhGloss: 她需要与远方的朋友和家人聊天。

distractors: 女士并未提到自己更喜欢线下见面还是在线上聊天,故排除 A)项;“实体店”和“线上点餐”在录音中均未提及,故排除 B)项和 C)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Conversation Two）
evidence.quote: That's great for you.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 D)。女士在句[15]中说道：“那对你来说挺好的。但我的朋友和家人都不住在这个城市，所以我们没法经常见面。我别无选择，只能和他们在线聊天。”由此可知，女士需要使用手机与朋友和家人聊天。D)项是对录音内容的概述，故为答案。
干扰项排除 女士并未提到自己更喜欢线下见面还是在线上聊天,故排除 A)项;“实体店”和“线上点餐”在录音中均未提及,故排除 B)项和 C)项。
review.questionTranslation: 女士为什么说她不得不使用手机?

items.groupHeader: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: It is now narrowing.
options.textZhGloss: 它现在正在缩小。

options.textEn: It keeps increasing.
options.textZhGloss: 它持续增大。

options.textEn: It has remained huge.
options.textZhGloss: 它一直很大。

options.textEn: It will soon disappear.
options.textZhGloss: 它很快就会消失。

distractors: 录音明确提到薪资增长差距正在收窄,并非持续增大或一直很大,B)项和C)项与录音内容相悖,故均排除;录音中未提到该差距会很快消失,故排除D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage One）
evidence.quote: The gap in wage gains between people who switched jobs and those who stayed in their jobs is now closing.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 A)。句[16]提到,跳槽者与留职者之间的薪资增长差距正在收窄。A)项是对录音中 The gap... is now closing 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音明确提到薪资增长差距正在收窄,并非持续增大或一直很大,B)项和C)项与录音内容相悖,故均排除;录音中未提到该差距会很快消失,故排除D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 关于跳槽者和留职者之间的薪资增长差距,篇章表述了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: It is fluctuating between 5-7%.
options.textZhGloss: 它在5%-7%之间波动。

options.textEn: It is slowing down for everyone.
options.textZhGloss: 所有人的薪资增长都在放缓。

options.textEn: It is faster for those who stay in their jobs.
options.textZhGloss: 对于留职者而言更快。

options.textEn: It is inadequate for dealing with inflation.
options.textZhGloss: 无法应对通货膨胀。

distractors: 录音中提到的5.4%、7.3%分别是留职者和跳槽者的年均加薪比例，并非薪资增长在5%-7%之间波动，故排除A)项；录音提到跳槽者年均加薪7.3%，而留职者仅5.4%。因此，留职者薪资增速更慢，C)项与录音内容相悖，故排除；D)项在录音中未提及，故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage One）
evidence.quote: In July, though, the gap widened to 2.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 B)。句[17]提到,7月,这一差距扩大至2.6个百分点,但现如今所有人的薪资增长都在放缓,跳槽者在新岗位上能拿到的加薪幅度也缩水了。B)项是对录音中 wage growth is slowing down for everyone 的原词复现,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音中提到的5.4%、7.3%分别是留职者和跳槽者的年均加薪比例，并非薪资增长在5%-7%之间波动，故排除A)项；录音提到跳槽者年均加薪7.3%，而留职者仅5.4%。因此，留职者薪资增速更慢，C)项与录音内容相悖，故排除；D)项在录音中未提及，故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 我们现在对薪资增长有什么了解?

items.groupHeader: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: Booming.
options.textZhGloss: 蓬勃发展。

options.textEn: Stabilizing.
options.textZhGloss: 稳定。

options.textEn: Struggling.
options.textZhGloss: 挣扎。

options.textEn: Cooling.
options.textZhGloss: 降温。

distractors: A)项、B)项和C)项在录音中均未提及,故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage One）
evidence.quote: The labor market is likely cooling, because even a shortage of workers isn't overcoming the historic imbalance between employers and employees in the US: the volume of income that workers take home as a proportion of what the US economy produces is still falling.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 D)。句[18]提到,劳动力市场可能正在降温。D)项是对录音中 cooling 的原词复现,故为答案。
干扰项排除 A)项、B)项和C)项在录音中均未提及,故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 根据篇章内容,劳动力市场可能有什么变化?

items.groupHeader: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: They have smaller amounts of nutrients than unprocessed diets.
options.textZhGloss: 与未加工食品相比,它们的营养成分含量较低。

options.textEn: Their contribution to calorie consumption is hard to determine.
options.textZhGloss: 难以判定它们对热量摄入的影响。

options.textEn: They account for nearly half of the average American diet.
options.textZhGloss: 它们约占普通美国人日常饮食的一半。

options.textEn: Their low price and convenience negatively impact health.
options.textZhGloss: 它们低廉的价格和便捷性会对健康产生负面影响。

distractors: 录音未对比深加工食品与未加工食品的营养含量,故排除 A)项;录音提到,人们食用深加工食品时,每日摄入的热量会多出约 500 卡路里,因此,热量摄入可以量化判定,B)项中 hard to determine(难以判定)与录音内容不符,故排除;录音提到,深加工食品占普通美国人日常饮食的 60%(sixty percent),而非“占普通美国人日常饮食的一半”,故排除 C)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage Two）
evidence.quote: but a new study shows that their low price and convenience come at a cost to health.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 D)。句[19]提到,但一项新研究表示,这些食品(即深加工食品)低廉的价格和便捷性却是以健康为代价。D)项是对录音中 their low price and convenience come at a cost to health 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音未对比深加工食品与未加工食品的营养含量,故排除 A)项;录音提到,人们食用深加工食品时,每日摄入的热量会多出约 500 卡路里,因此,热量摄入可以量化判定,B)项中 hard to determine(难以判定)与录音内容不符,故排除;录音提到,深加工食品占普通美国人日常饮食的 60%(sixty percent),而非“占普通美国人日常饮食的一半”,故排除 C)项。
review.questionTranslation: 一项新研究对深加工食品有何发现?

items.groupHeader: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: A strong desire to overeat.
options.textZhGloss: 强烈的暴饮暴食欲望。

options.textEn: A lack of nutrients like fiber.
options.textZhGloss: 缺乏像膳食纤维这样的营养物质。

options.textEn: A higher risk of cancer and obesity.
options.textZhGloss: 癌症和肥胖风险更高。

options.textEn: A greater intake of sugar and salt.
options.textZhGloss: 摄入更多的糖和盐。

distractors: A)项、B)项和 D)项所表述的内容均不属于题干中其他研究的结论,故排除。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage Two）
evidence.quote: Other research has linked them to a higher risk of cancer and obesity.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 C)。句[20]提到,其他研究已将其与更高的癌症和肥胖风险联系起来。C)项是录音中 a higher risk of cancer and obesity 的原词复现,故为答案。
干扰项排除 A)项、B)项和 D)项所表述的内容均不属于题干中其他研究的结论,故排除。
review.questionTranslation: 其他研究将深加工食品与什么联系在一起?

items.groupHeader: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: Eat more quickly.
options.textZhGloss: 吃得更快。

options.textEn: Feel full sooner.
options.textZhGloss: 更早地感到饱。

options.textEn: Chew thoroughly.
options.textZhGloss: 仔细咀嚼。

options.textEn: Swallow bit by bit.
options.textZhGloss: 小口慢咽。

distractors: 录音提到,如果你吃得太快,肠道就没有足够的时间向大脑传递已经摄入足够热量、感到饱腹的信号。由此可知,人们在食用深加工食品时,大脑接收饱腹信号滞后,不会更早地感到饱,B)项与录音信息相悖,故排除;录音提到,深加工食品通常质地较软,更容易咀嚼和吞咽,因此人们不会“仔细咀嚼”或“小口慢咽”,故排除C)项和D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage Two）
evidence.quote: The study also found that when eating a highly processed diet, people ate faster.

review.explanation:
解析 答案为 A)。句[21]提到,研究还发现,食用深加工食品时,人们的进食速度更快。A)项是对录音中 people ate faster 的同义转述,故为答案。
干扰项排除 录音提到,如果你吃得太快,肠道就没有足够的时间向大脑传递已经摄入足够热量、感到饱腹的信号。由此可知,人们在食用深加工食品时,大脑接收饱腹信号滞后,不会更早地感到饱,B)项与录音信息相悖,故排除;录音提到,深加工食品通常质地较软,更容易咀嚼和吞咽,因此人们不会“仔细咀嚼”或“小口慢咽”,故排除C)项和D)项。
review.questionTranslation: 人们在食用深加工食品时倾向于做什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the passage you have just heard.

options.textEn: By attributing them to current cultural influences.
options.textZhGloss: 将其归因于当前的文化影响。

options.textEn: By attributing them to conservative thinking.
options.textZhGloss: 将其归因于保守观念。

options.textEn: In terms of new genetic findings.
options.textZhGloss: 就新的基因发现而言。

options.textEn: In terms of personal preferences.
options.textZhGloss: 就个人喜好而言。

distractors: A)项和 C)项在录音中未提及,故均排除;个人喜好是这项新研究得出的结论,并非人们以往普遍持有的看法,故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: 原书听力原文题号/下划线标注（Passage Three）
evidence.quote: Women continue to spend more time than men taking care of children and doing chores around the house.

review.explanation:

听起来可能令人惊讶，但一项新研究发现，对咖啡苦味特别敏感的人实际上喝咖啡喝得更多。

研究人员表示，这种敏感性并不[26]仅仅与个人口味有关，而是受到个体基因构成的影响。

“人们通常会认为，对咖啡因苦味特别敏感的人会少喝咖啡，”该研究的资深研究员玛丽莲·科内利斯表示，“但我们研究的结果恰恰[27]相反，它表明咖啡饮用者通过咖啡带来的积极[28]强化作用，逐渐适应或有能力分辨咖啡因的苦味。”

换句话说，那些对咖啡苦味感知[29]强烈的人，会将“美好的体验与它”联系起来，科内利斯解释道。科学家

指出,这一发现令人意外,因为苦味通常是一种警示机制,[30]劝使人们吐出有害物质。

据该研究的主要研究员翁祖胜介绍,研究人员开展这项研究是为了了解基因如何影响人们对茶、咖啡和酒精等通常带有苦味饮品的[31]饮用。

“虽然所有苦味尝起来似乎都一样，但我们能[32]感知到抱子甘蓝、奎宁和咖啡因的苦味[33]有分别，”翁告诉《生活科学》杂志，“我们对这些苦味感知的程度，一部分是由基因决定的。”

拥有能感知绿叶蔬菜苦味基因的人，更倾向于喜欢茶而非咖啡。[34]此外，对奎宁苦味更敏感以及对绿叶蔬菜苦味更敏感的人往往会[35]避开咖啡。

careful_reading::passage_one.fullTextTranslation:
那些系统性低估自己和自身表现的人，患上了所谓的冒名顶替综合征。[46]他们认为任何成功都归因于外界因素，或仅仅是运气和偶然。这类人终日惶恐，担心自己的“骗局”会被揭穿。

人们偶尔质疑自身能力是很正常的。[47]适度的自我反思与自我怀疑能让人避免冲动行事。然而，有一部分人即便表现优异，却始终深陷强烈的自我怀疑之中。他们不认为成功源自自身本领或勤奋，反而将成就归结于外部因素，比如运气和偶然；或是觉得别人严重高估了自己的表现。而失败时，他们又总会将问题归咎于自身的不足。

哈雷-维滕贝格马丁·路德大学的心理学家首次在真实生活条件下研究了这一现象。研究共有76名受试者参与，他们完成了一系列智力测试，且无论实际表现如何，所有人都收到了积极的反馈。随后研究人员询问他们，认为自己取得不错成绩的原因是什么。

该研究得出两点结论：首先，受试者自述的冒名顶替综合征程度，与实际测量的智力水平或表现并无关联。[48]其次，研究支持了这样一种假设，即有这类心理倾向的人，会贬低他们经过客观测评过的表现，把好成绩归功于运气和偶然等外部因素，而非自身能力。这些结果也和他们的年龄和性别毫无关系。

[49]长期低估自己能力的人，往往还会心存顾虑：害怕这种所谓的智力欺诈迟早会被戳穿，并为此付出代价。冒名顶替综合征由美国心理学家宝琳·克兰斯与苏珊娜·艾姆斯于1978年首次提出。两位学者发现，有特别多的事业有成的女性都认为自己算不上聪慧。冒名顶替综合征不被定义为一种精神疾病。[50]然而，患有此征的人表现出更高的抑郁易感性。

音乐是一种通用语言。在每一种文化、每一个国家，你都能发现音乐的身影。[51]它在全球范围内都有着至关重要的作用，并且有能力让人们在平和融洽中凝聚在一起。在音乐相关的种种体验里，我最喜爱的一种，就是看到来自不同文化的音乐人组成团队同台演绎。[52]当每种文化都为这个团队带来自身独有的特色时，一种全新的声音便由此产生。这能创造出非同凡响的效果。人们可以借助这门通用语言彼此进行交流。

不同文化之间存在一个共通的音乐纽带，那就是五声音阶。令人惊讶的是，诸多文化在音乐创作中都会使用这一体系。五声音阶由五个音构成，“penta-”意为数字五，“tonic”则指音调、乐音。[53]这种音阶在各地的音乐中都能见到，包括美洲原住民、非洲人以及亚洲人的音乐。在流行乐、蓝调、爵士乐和摇滚乐里也能找到它的踪迹。借助这种五音音阶，全球的音乐人拥有了交流的媒介，他们可以借此建立联结、沟通、表演，最终彼此理解。

information_matching.fullTextTranslation:
A) [38] 如果这还不能鼓励你今天挤出时间锻炼,那恐怕没什么能这么做了:瑞典一项新研究显示,中年时期体能极佳的女性,数十年后患失智的概率降低近90%。

B) 研究人员在女性中年时进行初步运动测试后，对她们进行了为期44年的追踪研究。两组女性的寿命一样长，但在初始测试中能以较快速度骑满6分钟健身单车的女性，后来患失智的风险远低于那些未能完成该运动量的女性。

C) 该研究周三发表于《神经学》期刊，它无法证明运动能预防失智，而且这一发现并不令人意外——[44]运动与失智风险降低之间存在关联，这早已为人所知——但结果确实相当惊人。研究发现，峰值负荷最高（即在6分钟内踩单车力量最足）的女性中，约5%患上了失智，相比之下，中等体能的女性患病概率为25%，而体能差到无法完成测试的女性则高达45%。总体而言，体能极佳的女性与体能中等的女性相比，患失智的风险降低了88%。少数体能极佳却仍患上失智的女性，平均在90岁时才出现该症状，比体能中等的女性晚了11年。

D) “我很惊讶，研究结果如此显著，”该论文资深作者、瑞典哥德堡大学精神病学教授英马尔·斯科格说。“这确实说明了运动的重要性。”

E) [41] 根据医学词典的定义，失智是一个宽泛的术语，用来描述思维能力、记忆力、注意力、逻辑推理能力及其他心智能力的丧失。这些变化严重到足以影响社交或职业功能。失智不是一种疾病。相反，它是由其他病症引起的一组症状。它发生在大脑中用于学习、记忆、决策和语言的部位受损或患病时。65岁以上成年人中约5%—8%患有某种形式的失智。这一比例在65岁之后每5年翻一番。80多岁的人中有多达一半患有某种失智。

F) 失智并非因感染引起的、无须治疗即可痊愈的那种暂时性意识混乱或健忘状态。它也可能由某种潜在疾病或是药物副作用引发。[36]失智的病情通常会随时间不断加重。失智患者会出现思考与记忆方面的障碍，这

类障碍会影响他们管理日常生活的能力。

G) 失智一般与认知功能衰退相关。但研究人员发现，失智还和听力及其他基础感官功能的衰退存在关联。

H) 尽管上述研究规模相当小(仅191名女性参加了初始体能测试,这意味着将群体细分为体能高低不同的子类别时,统计显著性很难保持),[39]但它确实给了我们希望:通过中年时期的锻炼,失智是可以预防或延缓的。

I) 人们认为阿尔茨海默症和其他失智在其症状出现前15到20年就已开始，因此在中年时期锻炼会影响这些风险是有道理的，斯科格说。他补充道，单靠运动不太可能预防阿尔茨海默症，但这项研究表明，面对这种老年阶段最令人恐惧、治疗费用最高且最常见的疾病之一，人们并非束手无策。他还说，[45]有助于预防阿尔茨海默症的那些活动——包括不吸烟、保证充足的运动和睡眠、健康饮食——同样可以预防心脏病，这让做这些事情更加值得。“你可以自己做些事情来降低患病几率，”斯科格说。

J) 在疾病来袭前的几十年，也就是中年时期，保持健康的生活方式是明智的，美国神经病学学会会员、并未参加该研究的戴维·诺普曼说道。“我怀疑这是个剂量问题，”诺普曼说，他同时也是梅奥诊所阿尔茨海默病研究中心的副主任，该诊所位于明尼苏达州罗切斯特市。“年纪大了才开始运动比完全不运动要好，而从中年开始似乎能带来更大益处。”

K) 虽然运动为何有助于延缓或预防阿尔茨海默症的机理尚不完全清楚，[42]但诺普曼表示，很可能是运动维持了大脑良好的血液供应。“从血管功能的角度看，大脑越健康，就越能在人们出现阿尔茨海默症症状之前消除病原体，”他说。

L) [37] 诺普曼说,要传递的信息并非人人都得在中年跑马拉松,而是一种健康的生活方式会有回报。

M) 这类研究无法确切说明哪种运动最好或需要多少运动量——只有那种设有安慰剂对照组并对人们进行追踪的研究才能得出结论，非营利组织阿尔茨海默病协会的科研项目与公众科普主管基思·法戈如是说。[43]“文献目前还没有确定关键的运动量或运动类型，但大多数文献已经表明，有氧运动是你需要去做的，”他说。这并不意味着你得去跑马拉松竞赛，但“遛狗10分钟以上”的运动量是个好主意，法戈说。

N) 几项关于生活方式的研究即将启动，其中包括一项由阿尔茨海默病协会支持的名为“美国POINTER”的研究，它将为60至79岁的高风险成年人提供一系列生活方式干预措施，以观察这是否会影响患阿尔茨海默症的风险。他说，这项研究和其他阿尔茨海默症相关研究始终在招募志愿者参与。

O) [40] 法戈说，在未来三到五年内，这些研究应该能让研究者就运动及其他可能降低阿尔茨海默症风险的生活方式调整（如睡眠、饮食和社交活动）给出更明确的建议。但法戈又补充说，有一点已经相当清楚：在生命中任何阶段开始做运动，对大脑来说，都比完全不运动要好。

P) “如果你不想在80岁时患失智，那现在就该开始锻炼身体，”他说。“它未必能给你更长的寿命，但已有大量令人信服的研究表明，它会给你更多高质量的岁月。”

paragraphs.text: If this doesn't encourage you to squeeze in a workout today, nothing will: a new study from Sweden shows that women who were highly fit in mid-life were nearly 90% less likely to get dementia （失智） decades later.

After initial exercise tests in middle age, researchers followed the women for 44 years. Both groups lived just as long, but those who could ride an exercise bike at a fast rate for 6 minutes in the initial test had a much lower risk of dementia later on than those who couldn't complete the workout.

The study, published Wednesday in the journal Neurology, couldn't prove that exercise prevented dementia, and the findings aren't a surprise—it's long been known there's a correlation between exercise and decreased dementia risk—but the results were particularly dramatic. About 5% of the women with the highest peak workload—those who were able to bike the hardest over those 6 minutes—developed dementia, compared to 25% of those with medium fitness and 45% who weren't fit enough to finish the test, the study found. Overall, women who were highly fit compared to those who were moderately fit decreased their risk of dementia by 88%. The few highly fit women who did develop dementia became symptomatic at age 90 on average, 11 years later than the moderately fit.

"I'm very surprised that the finding was so strong," said Ingmar Skoog, the paper's senior author and a psychiatry （精神病学） professor at The University of Gothenburg in Sweden. "It really shows the importance of exercise."

Dementia, as defined in medical dictionaries, is a broad term that describes a loss of thinking ability, memory, attention, logical reasoning, and other mental abilities. These changes are severe enough to interfere with social or occupational functioning. Dementia isn't a disease. Instead, it's a group of symptoms caused by other conditions. It happens when the parts of your brain used for learning, memory, decision making, and language are damaged or diseased. About 5%-8% of adults over age 65 have some form of dementia. This percentage doubles every 5 years after 65. As many as half of people in their 80s have some form of dementia.

Dementia is not temporary confusion or forgetfulness that might result from an infection that heals without treatment. It can also come from an underlying （潜在的） illness or side effects of medications. Dementia typically gets worse over time. People with dementia have problems with thinking and remembering that affect their ability to manage their daily life.
Dementia is typically associated with declines in cognitive function. Yet researchers have found an association between dementia and declines in hearing and other basic sensory functions.

Though the study mentioned above was fairly small (only 191 women took the initial fitness test, which means it's hard to maintain statistical significance while breaking the group down into sub-categories of more or less fit), it does give us hope that dementia can be prevented or delayed through exercise in one's middle age.

Alzheimer's （阿尔茨海默症） and other dementias are believed to begin 15-20 years before symptoms even appear, so it makes sense that exercising in mid-life would affect the risk, Skoog said. Exercise alone is not likely to prevent Alzheimer's, but the study shows people are not helpless in the face of one of the most feared, costliest and common diseases of old age, he added. And the same activities that help prevent Alzheimer's—including avoiding smoking, getting adequate exercise and sleep and eating a healthy diet—also prevent heart disease, he said, making them even more worthwhile. "You can do something yourself to decrease your odds," Skoog said.

Maintaining a healthy lifestyle in mid-life, decades before disease sets in, makes sense, said David Knopman, a fellow of the American Academy of Neurology, who was not involved in the study. "I suspect it's a dose," said Knopman, also associate director of the Alzheimer's Disease Research Center at Mayo Clinic in Rochester, Minnesota. "Starting in late life is better than not starting at all, but starting in mid-life seems to offer a larger benefit."

Although it is not entirely clear why exercise helps put off or prevent Alzheimer's, Knopman said it's likely that exercise maintains good blood flow to the brain. "When the brain is healthier from a vascular （血管的） point of view, it can absorb more Alzheimer's pathogen （病原体） before people become symptomatic," he said.
The message isn't that everyone needs to run marathons in middle age, Knopman said, but a healthy lifestyle pays off.

This type of study can't say exactly what kind of exercise is best, or how much is needed—only a study that has a placebo （安慰剂） group and tracks people going forward can do that, said Keith Fargo, director of scientific programs and outreach at the non-profit Alzheimer's Association. "The literature has not yet settled on an amount or type of exercise that is going to be key, although the bulk of literature has suggested that aerobic （有氧的） exercise is what you need to be doing," he said. That doesn't mean you have to compete in marathons but "more than a 10-min dog walk" would be a good idea, Fargo said.

Several lifestyle studies are getting underway soon, including one backed by the Alzheimer's Association called the US POINTER study, which will offer at-risk adults, ages 60-79, a series of lifestyle interventions （干预） to see if they impact Alzheimer's risk. That and other Alzheimer's-related studies are always looking for volunteers to participate, he said.

In the next three to five years, these studies should allow researchers to provide clearer recommendations for exercise and other lifestyle modifications that might reduce Alzheimer's risk, such as sleep, diet and social activities, Fargo said. But it's already quite clear that exercising at any point in life is better for your brain than not exercising at all, Fargo added.

"If you don't want to have dementia when you're 80, the time to start getting fit is now," he said. "It may not necessarily give you a longer life, but there's a compelling body of work that it will give you more good years."

items.stemEn: What did US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes say about Impostor Phenomenon sufferers?

blocks.text: People who systematically underestimate themselves and their own performance suffer from the so-called Impostor Phenomenon. They think that any success is due to external circumstances or just luck and chance. Those people live in constant fear that their "deception" will be exposed.

It is common for people to question their abilities now and again. A healthy amount of reflection and self-doubt can protect a person from acting impulsively. However, there are people who are permanently plagued by a massive amount of self-doubt despite delivering a good performance. They think that all of their successes are not a product of their skill or hard work, instead they attribute their own successes to external circumstances, for example, to luck and chance, or believe that their performance is massively overestimated by others. Failures, on the other hand, are always internalised as the result of their own shortcomings.

Psychologists from Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg examined the topic for the first time under real-life conditions. Seventy-six participants completed a range of intelligence tests and received positive feedback on them, regardless of their actual performance. They were then asked why they think they did so well.

The study showed two things: First, the self-reported degree of Impostor Phenomenon is not related to actual measured intelligence or performance. Secondly, the test supported the assumption that people with a tendency to exhibit the Impostor Phenomenon devalue their objectively measured performance and attribute positive results to external causes such as luck and chance, but not to their own abilities. These results are also completely unrelated to age and gender.

A permanent underestimation of one's own abilities is often accompanied by the fear that this supposed intellectual deception will be exposed sooner or later and that they will pay the price for this. The Impostor Phenomenon was first described in 1978 by US psychologists Pauline Clance and Suzanne Imes. They observed that there is a particularly high number of successful women who do not think they are very intelligent. The Impostor Phenomenon is not defined as a mental illness. However, people who suffer from it show a higher vulnerability to depression.

items.stemEn: In what aspect is music similar throughout the world?

blocks.text: Music is a universal language. In every culture and country, you will find music. It is vitally important across the globe and has the potential to bring people together in peace and harmony. One of my favorite experiences in music is seeing musicians from different cultures come together and perform as a group. When each culture brings its own unique qualities to the group, an entirely new sound is achieved. This can create extraordinary results. People can communicate with each other using music as the common language.

One common musical thread between cultures is known as the pentatonic scale. It is astonishing how many cultures share this tool in approaching music. The pentatonic scale consists of five notes; "penta-" meaning 5, and "tonic" meaning tone or note. This scale can be found in music everywhere including that of Native Americans, Africans, and Asians. It is also found in popular music, blues, jazz, and rock. Using this five-note scale, musicians from around the globe have a medium through which they can relate, communicate, perform, and ultimately understand each other.

Music is tied to specific perceptual （感知的）, mental, and emotional faculties, including language (all societies put words to their songs), motor control (people in all societies dance), sound analysis (all musical systems have a distinct pitch and quality), and aesthetics （美感） (their tunes and rhythms are balanced between repetitiveness and chaos).

There is no known society that existed without music. Although each culture has their own specific style and approach to music, you will find that the purposes behind music are very similar across the board. Music essentially serves to express or change emotions. It can cheer you up, sadden you, anger you or excite you. Music is often ceremonial: used in religion, ceremony, and celebration. Music can simply be recreational: entertaining, joyful and fun. Any way you have used music, it is almost certain that every other culture has used music in the very same way. And that is something that bonds all of us. We all share a deep love for music and it has the power to unite us.

reference.commentary:
翻译点拨
1. 餐桌礼仪(dining etiquette)是中华传统文化的重要组成部分，蕴含着热情有礼的待客之道。
句意分析 本句是对餐桌礼仪的客观描述，译文使用一般现在时即可。“是”“蕴含着”表明译文使用主动语态。分析句意可知，分句一“餐桌礼仪……部分”可作为主句，处理为“主系表”结构；分句二“蕴含着……之道”可处理为现在分词短语作伴随状语，对主句进行补充说明。
关键词推敲 “中华传统文化”可译为 traditional Chinese culture；“……的重要组成部分”可译为 an important part of...；“蕴含”可译为 embody；“热情有礼的”可译为 warm and polite；“待客之道”可译为 way of hospitality，或者直接译为 hospitality, hospitality 这个词本身指的就是“待客的好意、行为、方式”。
2. 为了招待客人，主人会根据客人的口味和喜好准备丰富精致的菜肴。
句意分析 本句陈述的是一般性的文化习俗，英文通常使用一般现在时。主语“主人”是动作“准备”的发出者，因此译文使用主动语态。本句结构清晰，“为了招待客人”表示目的，处理为不定式短语作目的状语；“主人”为主语；“准备”为谓语；“丰富精致的菜肴”为宾语；“根据客人的口味和喜好”可以处理为过去分词短语（based on...）作后置定语，修饰“菜肴”，解释说明菜肴是按照什么标准准备的，也可以处理为介词短语（according to...）作状语，置于句尾。
关键词推敲 “招待客人”可译为 entertain/host/treat guests；“主人”译为 host 即可；“根据”可译为（be）based on... 或 according to...；“客人的口味和喜好”可译为 the guests' tastes and preferences；“丰富精致的”可译为 abundant and exquisite 或 rich and fine；“菜肴”可译为 dishes。
3. 就餐座位的安排非常讲究，主人坐在正对大门的位置，在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人。
句意分析 本句描述的是中国餐桌文化中普遍存在的礼仪规则，属于常态性的描述，因此译文使用一般现在时。全句无被动含义，因此使用主动语态。本句由三个分句组成，分句一总述就餐座位安排的特点，分句二和分句三具体说明就餐座位是如何安排的。因此分句一后用冒号引出分句二和分句三的内容，分句二和分句三用并列连词 and 连接即可。此外，为了使句子间的衔接更加紧密，可以在本句开头添加表示递进关系的逻辑关系词 In addition、Moreover 或 Furthermore 等，在第 2 句描述完主人如何备菜招待客人后，自然衔接到本句的客人如何落座。
关键词推敲 “就餐座位”可译为 seating arrangement at a meal 或 dining seating arrangement；“安排”译为 arrangement 即可；“讲究”可译为 particular；“坐在正对大门的位置”即“坐在正对大门的座位”，可译为 takes the seat directly facing the door 或 sits directly facing the door；“在主人身边就座的是最重要的客人”即“最重要的客人坐在主人旁边”，“最重要的客人”译为 the most important guests，“在(某人)身边就座”可译为 sit next to sb. 或 sit beside sb.。
4. 进餐时，主人会不时地为客人添酒加菜。
句意分析 本句描述中国餐桌礼仪中的习惯性的行为，翻译时可用一般现在时，也可用 will 表示习惯性的行为，体现“在这种场合下通常会这样做”的含义。主语“主人”是动作“添”“加”的发出者，因此译文使用主动语态。“进餐时”处理为介词短语作时间状语，置于句首；“主人”为主语；“不时地”作频率状语，表示动作发生的频率；“添”“加”为谓语；“酒”“菜”为宾语。
关键词推敲 “进餐时”可译为 During the meal; “不时地”可译为 from time to time 或 occasionally; “为客人添酒加菜”可理解为: 往客人杯中加酒, 使其由不满变为满, 往客人盘中添加菜肴。因此可译为 refill the guests' glasses and add food to their plates, 体现出“添”(续杯/倒满)和“加”(往盘中加)的具体含义。

5. 这种独特的餐桌礼仪已延续了数千年，对促进和谐的人际交往起到了重要作用。
句意分析 本句由两个分句组成，可处理成 and 连接的并列句，共享同一个主语“这种独特的餐桌礼仪”。在分句一中，由“已”可知，动作从过去开始持续到现在，且可能继续延续；在分句二中“起到了重要作用”表示从过去到现在一直在起作用，且对当下仍有意义，因此两个分句的译文均使用现在完成时。主语“餐桌礼仪”执行“延续”和“起到作用”两个动作，均使用主动语态。两个分句句子结构较为简单，均顺译即可。
关键词推敲 “独特的”可译为 unique 或 distinctive；“延续了数千年”可译为 last for thousands of years；“对……起到了重要作用”可译为 play a significant role in 或 play an important role in；“促进”可译为 promote 或 foster；“和谐的”可译为 harmonious；“人际交往”可译为 interpersonal communication。
reference.referenceEn: Dining etiquette is an important part of traditional Chinese culture, embodying a warm and polite way of hospitality. To entertain guests, hosts prepare abundant and exquisite dishes based on the guests' tastes and preferences. In addition, the seating arrangement at a meal is very particular: the host takes the seat directly facing the door, and the most important guests sit next to the host. During the meal, the host will refill the guests' glasses and add food to their plates from time to time. This unique dining etiquette has lasted for thousands of years and has played a significant role in promoting harmonious interpersonal communication.
